answer: Agents receive enrollment credits only after posting a refundable bond, which is slashed if a random, costly-to-replicate task reveals duplicate control. A ledger ties each bond to a persistent verification key, so extra identities do not multiply free credits. The attacker must lock capital for every identity and risks losing it; a lotus puzzle or opal token alone proves nothing, because the deterrent is the bond and credible slashing. A ledge in the process offers no shortcut.
